summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) discusses the miracles of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and prominent figures in early Islamic history. The speaker covers several miraculous events, including the story of Suraqa ibn Malik, who pursued the Prophet during his migration from Mecca to Medina but witnessed miraculous signs that convinced him of the Prophet's divine mission. The lecture details how Suraqa later received a letter of safe passage and eventually embraced Islam at the conquest of Mecca, after which the Prophet prophesied that he would wear the bracelets of Kisra (the Persian Emperor)—a prophecy fulfilled during Caliph Umar's time when the Persian Empire was conquered. The speaker also discusses the prophecy regarding Hasan ibn Ali, the Prophet's grandson, who would unite Muslims during a time of division. The lecture extensively addresses the historical tensions between Ali ibn Abi Talib and Muawiyah following the murder of Uthman ibn Affan, clarifying misconceptions about their disagreement and emphasizing that both were companions of the Prophet with the same essential goals but differing on methodology. The speaker highlights how fabricated narrations arose from political factions, warning against accepting unverified reports from both sides of historical disputes.
suggested_title: Miracles of the Prophet and Early Islamic History: Suraqa ibn Malik and the Conflict Between Ali and Muawiyah
catchy_title: When the Prophet's Enemy Became His Follower
